diagnostic_evidence.quote: \bv \mapsto \norm{\bv \cdot \bn}_{L^q(\Gamma)}\qquad \text{is a norm on the  rigid deformations $\mathcal{R}(\Omega)$}

issues.failure_explanation: Verifying Assumption assump:dom for a rigid deformation pi(x)=Ax+b requires excluding pi·bn=0 a.e. on Gamma with pi nonzero. On a face with constant normal nu_i this yields only (Ax+b)·nu_i=0 on H_i, i.e. Anu_i=0 and b·nu_i=0. For two non-collinear normals in d=3 this forces A=0 (a skew 3x3 matrix is a cross-product matrix; w x nu_i=0 for i=1,2 implies w=0) but leaves b arbitrary in the direction nu_1 x nu_2. Counterexample: Omega=(0,1)^3, Gamma_1 the face {x_1=1} (nu_1=e_1), Gamma_2 the face {x_2=1} (nu_2=e_2); the translation rho=e_3 satisfies rho·bn=0 on Gamma_1 u Gamma_2 but rho is nonzero, so the map in assump:dom is not a norm and the Korn inequality eq:kornetto0 fails for this Gamma (take u=rho). The proof instead assumes the strictly stronger condition 'pi=0 on Gamma', which does not follow from the hypothesis; even in d=2, where the statement is true, that step is unjustified (the correct argument uses Anu_i=0 and b·nu_i=0, not pi=0).

failure_location.quote: Let $A\in\R^{d\times d}$ be skew-symmetric,  $b\in\R^{d}$, and suppose that $\pi(x)\\coloneqq Ax+b$ satisfies $\pi=0$ on $\Gamma$, whereby $\pi=0$ on $H_{1}\cup H_{2}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the two-hyperplane hypothesis by d affine hyperplanes H_1,...,H_d whose normals nu_1,...,nu_d span R^d (equivalently, require the normals occurring on Gamma to span R^d), and correct the proof step to the valid implication (Ax+b)·nu_i=0 on H_i implies Anu_i=0 and b·nu_i=0, which then yields A=0 and b=0. The full polyhedral boundary case and the main theorem remain covered.
issues.overall_effect: The corollary as stated, and the accompanying figure caption claim, are false for d=3: for a 3D polyhedral domain with slip imposed on only two non-collinear faces, rho -> ||rho·bn||_{L^q(Gamma)} is not a norm on rigid deformations and the Korn inequality eq:kornetto0 is unavailable. Consequently the mixed-boundary-condition extension discussed in Remark rmk:mixed-bc is not justified for such Gamma in 3D. Theorem thm:korn-n itself is correct, and the main theorem thm:main-unsteady (which uses Gamma=∂Omega, where the norm property is verified directly in Lemma lem:h-norm) is unaffected.
issues.title: Corollary cor:polyhedral is false in dimension 3 (two non-collinear face normals do not suffice), and its proof assumes the strictly stronger condition pi=0 on Gamma instead of pi·bn=0
issues.why_classification: The corollary is a false statement in the paper's dimension d=3, so the error is substantive; however the repair is contained (a spanning-normals hypothesis plus a small correction of the proof step), yields a comparable result, and leaves the main theorem and thm:korn-n untouched, so no new global proof architecture or major loss is involved.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Thus, there is a function $\xi \in L^{8/(d+4)}(I;L^2(\Omega))$ and a (non--relabelled) subsequence such that \xi^k \wconv \xi \quad \text{ weakly in } L^{8/(d+4)}(I;L^2(\Omega))

issues.failure_explanation: The estimate in Lemma lem:p-est controls only delta_k^2 sum_j ||pi^k_j||^{8/(d+4)}; it does not control the time primitive xi^k(t)=int_0^t pi^k(s) ds. Counterexample in d=3 (exponent 8/7): the piecewise constant sequence pi^k with ||pi^k_j||_{L^2(Omega)}=(delta_k T)^{-1/2} for every j satisfies delta_k^2 sum_j ||pi^k_j||^{8/7}=(delta_k T)^{3/7} <= c, i.e. the conclusion of lem:p-est, but xi^k(t)=t*pi^k_j yields ||xi^k||_{L^{8/7}(I;L^2)}^{8/7}=T^{15/7}(7/15)(delta_k T)^{-4/7} -> infinity. Hence eq:est-press-4 is unproved, the weak limit xi and the convergence of int_0^T pi^k phi^k to -int_0^T xi d_t phi are not established, and the missing argument (sum the discrete equation in time to bound grad xi^k in L^{8/(d+4)}(I;H^{-1}), then use ||v||_{L^2_0} <= C ||grad v||_{H^{-1}}) is nontrivial.

failure_location.quote: By Lemma~\ref{lem:p-est} we have \begin{align}\label{eq:est-press-4} \norm{\xi^k}_{L^{8/(d+4)}(I;L^2(\Omega))} \leq c, \end{align} uniformly in $k$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Sum the discrete momentum equation in time up to t to obtain grad xi^k(t) as the sum of (bu_0 - bu^k(t)) and the summed spatial terms, giving grad xi^k bounded in L^{8/(d+4)}(I;H^{-1}(Omega)) from the existing a priori bounds; then ||xi^k||_{L^{8/(d+4)}(I;L^2_0)} <= C||grad xi^k||_{L^{8/(d+4)}(I;H^{-1})} yields eq:est-press-4 and the lemma. Alternatively, test the discrete equation with exactly divergence-free discrete functions so that the pressure term vanishes identically.
issues.overall_effect: The pressure convergence lemma is unsupported as written. Proposition prop:limit-eq uses it for the pressure term in the distributional limit equation and in the passage to the pressure-free formulation (the Scott-Zhang test functions are not divergence-free, so the pressure term only vanishes in the limit because div v=0), and the proofs of thm:main-unsteady and thm:main-unsteady-v rely on prop:limit-eq. The main result itself is pressure-free and repairable, but the distributional pressure formulation (step 1 of prop:limit-eq) and the pressure regularity claims in Remark rmk:pressure-formulation are unsupported as written.
issues.title: Lemma lem:unst-conv-pi: the uniform bound on the pressure primitive xi^k does not follow from the pressure estimate lem:p-est; the proof contains an invalid inference
issues.why_classification: The inference from lem:p-est to eq:est-press-4 is invalid (explicit counterexample), so the pressure lemma and everything using it are unproved as written; however a contained, standard repair (summed-equation pressure estimate or divergence-free test functions) restores the lemma and both main theorems without changing any regime, rate, or advertised guarantee, so the issue is more than minor but does not require new global proof architecture.
